fixes.explanation: Altars are a fair guess, baker. But nothing in these verses says a word about altars. Isaiah points at the people's own iniquities as the thing that built the barriers.
Right, baker. Isaiah says, "No one calls for justice; no one pleads his case honestly." That's a heavy line, and Isaiah says it plainly.

That's the exact opposite, friend. Isaiah says, "No one calls for justice; no one pleads his case honestly." Nobody is doing it honestly, not even a few. It's an easy one to flip when you're reading fast.
Feeling sick sounds bad enough, baker, but Isaiah goes further. He says, "Whoever eats their eggs will die…" That's how serious the picture is.
Neighbors are a fair guess, friend. But the voice says, "…our sins testify against us." The witness is their own sins.
The prophets are a natural guess, baker. But here the voice says, "…our sins testify against us." The sins themselves are the witness.
True, baker. The voice says, "Our transgressions are indeed with us, and we know our iniquities…" They name it themselves. I think that honest moment matters.
Yes, baker. Isaiah says, "…truth has stumbled in the public square…" Not in private, but in a public place. That's where Isaiah puts the stumble.
Temple courts are a fair guess, friend, but they're not named here. The verse says, "…truth has stumbled in the public square…" So the place is a public one.
A short fast is a fair thing to wonder about, friend, but it's not in this verse. Here Isaiah says, "The LORD looked and was displeased that there was no justice." Justice is what was missing.
His word is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't what this verse names. Isaiah says, "So His own arm brought salvation, and His own righteousness sustained Him." The arm is the answer.
Not quite, friend. Isaiah says He will come "…like a raging flood, driven by the breath of the LORD." So the breath of the LORD is exactly what drives it.

Yes, friend. The LORD declares, "The Redeemer will come to Zion…" After all that darkness, I think that's good news. Earlier the voice said salvation is far from them, and here is a promise that Someone will come.

That's right, baker. The LORD says the Redeemer comes "…to those in Jacob who turn from transgression…" The door is open to those who turn. Jacob here is the people called by the name Israel (Isaiah 48:1).
Prophets are a fair guess, friend, but they're not in this promise. The LORD says, "My Spirit will not depart from you…" It's His Spirit.
